title: Gaussian KL: closed form against Monte Carlo
goal:
Appendix B of the paper gives $-D_{KL}(q_\phi(z)\,\|\,p_\theta(z)) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^{J}\left(1 + \log\sigma_j^2 - \mu_j^2 - \sigma_j^2\right)$ for $q = \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2 I)$ and $p = \mathcal{N}(0, I)$.

Write two functions. `kl_closed_form(mu, logvar)` takes arrays of shape `(batch, J)` and returns the KL for each row, shape `(batch,)`. It takes `logvar` $= \log \sigma^2$ instead of $\sigma$, as most implementations do; the paper writes $\sigma$. `kl_monte_carlo(mu, logvar, eps)` estimates the same KL as the average of $\log q(z) - \log p(z)$ over `eps` of shape `(L, batch, J)`, with $z = \mu + \sigma \odot \epsilon$.
hints: The closed form is a sum over the last axis. Return the KL, which is the negative of the Appendix B expression.
For the Monte Carlo version, write `log_q` and `log_p` as sums over the last axis of the per-dimension Gaussian log densities, then average `log_q - log_p` over axis 0.
